clues.text: This city stands on a bend of a great river, the last good spot where boats from down south could land. A twin city faces it across the water.
clues.narrowing: Rules out lands far from the great river; puts the player at its last good boat landing, facing a twin city.

source.quote: The location was the last good point to land riverboats coming upriver due to the river valley's topography.

clues.text: Far north, with no large lakes near to soften the air, this place takes Arctic cold blasts head on. It is the coldest big city area in the whole land.
clues.narrowing: Rules out milder north lands; no lakes soften the air, so Arctic cold hits head on.

source.quote: Due to its northerly location and lack of large bodies of water to moderate the air, Saint Paul is sometimes subjected to cold Arctic air masses

clues.text: In 1849 a new territory was formed here, and this small river town was made its capital. It has kept that job ever since.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to a river town picked as a new territory's capital in 1849.

source.quote: The Minnesota Territory was created in 1849 with Saint Paul as the capital.

clues.text: On a hill over the river bend stands the state capitol, a grand hall clad in bright marble. Lawmakers have met in its rooms since the year 1905.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: a grand marble capitol on a hill over the river bend marks this city.

source.quote: replacing or repairing tens of thousands of pieces of marble on the exterior

clues.text: The leaders of Minnesota make its laws in this city, in the capitol on the hill. The state chief and the top court work there too.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the state's lawmakers and governor work in the capitol in this city.

source.quote: It houses the Minnesota Senate, Minnesota House of Representatives, the office of the attorney general and the office of the governor.

reveal.blurb: River traders and Dakota towns came first, and in 1849 a new territory made this river town its capital. Steamboats crowded its landing, and in 1905 a grand marble capitol rose on the hill. Mind the words: the building is the capitol, and the city is the capital. Saint Paul is the capital of Minnesota.
